assumptions: Universe: 402 FAA Primary Airports; every metric is a Percentile Score (0–100) among the Primary Airports that have it.
Pillar Weights (defaults): Demand Momentum 0.35, Capacity Pressure 0.40, Market Scale 0.25.
Demand Momentum = 0.60 × TAF enplanement CAGR FY2024→FY2035 (incl. international) + 0.40 × CY2024→CY2025 enplanement growth.
Capacity Pressure = 0.40 × class F Load Factor (12 months, Aug 2025–Jul 2026) + 0.30 × share of departures delayed ≥15 min + 0.30 × average taxi-out (12 months, Sep 2025–Aug 2026).
Market Scale = 0.70 × CY2025 enplanements + 0.30 × 2025 metro (CBSA) population.
Investment Opportunity Score = weighted geometric mean of the three Pillars (each floored at 1), so weakness in any one Pillar is penalised.
Missing metrics are imputed at the median (50th percentile): this pulls the Pillar toward the middle and can raise or lower an airport; such scores are Provisional and name the imputed metrics.
delay_share and taxi_out are left unmeasured for airports with fewer than 1,000 reporting-carrier departures in the On-Time window.
caveats: The Investment Opportunity Score is a screening signal: it identifies airports worth investigating and does not establish that a terminal renovation would be profitable (it has no project cost, terminal or gate utilisation, commercial revenue or feasibility data).
On-Time data covers only the largest (reporting) US carriers and domestic flights, so delay and taxi-out say nothing about international operations.
